Write a run's results to its folder

Source: R/results_files.R
gpq_write_results.Rd

Writes a gpq_results object to <output_dir>/<run_id>/: the results summary, issues and corrections to tables/, and the run metadata to metadata/, one CSV file for each table: results.csv, issues.csv and corrections.csv, and the eight metadata tables.

Usage

gpq_write_results(results, output_dir)

Arguments

results

A gpq_results object, such as gpq_check_conformance() returns.

output_dir

The folder that holds run folders, made if it doesn't exist.

Value

The run folder's path, invisibly.

Details

Every file has LF line endings, every text field quoted and a missing value an empty field. Text is written as UTF-8, except a value whose bytes aren't valid UTF-8, which is written as given. So gpq_read_results() reads back the same object. A run's files are written once. Before writing anything the call stops when the run folder already holds a file other than that run's own pre-flight files, which gpq_preflight() writes: reports/preflight.html and metadata/preflight.csv. The second must hold the results' pre-flight table byte for byte, and is then left as it is.

Examples

# MAGPlot's bundled specification has known pre-flight warnings, so this warning is expected.
results <- gpq_check_conformance(
  magp_example, magp_spec(),
  rules = magp_rules(), layers = 0:2
)
#> Warning: Pre-flight found 32 warning(s); see the returned table.
run_dir <- gpq_write_results(results, tempfile("runs"))
list.files(run_dir, recursive = TRUE)
#>  [1] "metadata/clashes.csv"       "metadata/inputs.csv"       
#>  [3] "metadata/preflight.csv"     "metadata/rules.csv"        
#>  [5] "metadata/run.csv"           "metadata/self_test.csv"    
#>  [7] "metadata/settings.csv"      "metadata/spec_manifest.csv"
#>  [9] "tables/corrections.csv"     "tables/issues.csv"         
#> [11] "tables/results.csv"
